claims.text: The baseline alloy is equiatomic MoNbTaW.
The initial MoNbTaW alloy is free from secondary phases.
The intervention adds approximately 1 at.% boron to MoNbTaW.
A tailored heat treatment will produce controlled in situ precipitation of nanoscale TaB2-like particles.
The precipitates will form a fine, homogeneous dispersion both along grain boundaries and within grains.
Trace boron induces heterogeneous nucleation of coherent or semicoherent boride nanoparticles.
The boride nanoparticles pin or otherwise impede dislocation motion.
The boride nanoparticles suppress grain-boundary sliding.
Suppression of dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will strengthen the alloy at high temperature and improve creep resistance.
A low precipitate volume fraction and nanoscale precipitate size will minimize adverse effects on room-temperature properties.
Relative to boron-free MoNbTaW, the modified alloy will show a 20–30% increase in high-temperature yield strength at approximately 1200°C and approximately 100 MPa.
Relative to boron-free MoNbTaW, the modified alloy will show a 20–30% improvement in creep resistance at approximately 1200°C and approximately 100 MPa.
The boron-modified alloy will retain statistically similar room-temperature strength relative to boron-free MoNbTaW.
The boron-modified alloy will retain statistically similar room-temperature ductility relative to boron-free MoNbTaW.
Over-precipitation, precipitate coarsening, or excessive grain-boundary segregation may cause grain-boundary embrittlement and degradation of room-temperature properties.
Conditions near 1200°C and 100 MPa are relevant to jet-turbine service.
